title: aiPHeed Food Insecurity Forecast Report
subtitle: Province Risk Level Trend
metadata: 2027 Q1 Lead-1 forecast issued 2026-10-01 (E168 food-insecurity risk forecast (probability of HIGH; not a measured rate))

E168 (e168-lgbm-1.0): latest provincial HFIAS survey level + constrained LightGBM change (five trigger groups, news inside groups) + calibration. Leads 1-3 meet the acceptance rule (Lead 1 accuracy 0.750 on 72 provincial forecasts; latest survey alone 0.625).

blocks.text: The number below is E168's forecast probability that the province is HIGH food-insecurity risk: that 50% or more of households are moderately or severely food insecure (FNRI HFIAS), from 0 to 1, HIGH at 0.50. E168 starts from the latest published provincial survey level and adds a constrained LightGBM forecast of the change from the five trigger groups. It is a forecast risk class, not a measured food-insecurity rate. Approved under the project acceptance rule (accuracy of at least 75% and better than the latest survey) at 1 to 3 quarters ahead.

items: In 2027 Q1, the food-insecurity risk (E168 forecast probability that 50% or more of households are moderately or severely food insecure; not a measured rate) for Quezon is 0.08 (LOW), rank 1 of 5.
The 2027 Q1 value is a Lead-1 forecast issued 2026-10-01 (the horizon that passed the reliability test); its outcome is not yet known.

blocks.text: Table 1 shows the food-insecurity risk (E168 forecast probability that 50% or more of households are moderately or severely food insecure; not a measured rate), its level and rank on the map, and the main factor for 2027 Q1, from the highest probability to the lowest.

blocks.label: Table 1
blocks.title: Risk Probability and Risk Level for Quezon, 2027 Q1
blocks.note: Risk level: HIGH at a probability of 0.50 and above, LOW below, as on the map; the rank is the map's ranking (tied values share a rank). The main factor is the indicator group with the largest relative influence on the food-price part of the forecast.

blocks.text: Each bar is a trigger group's relative influence (exact LightGBM contributions, rescaled to 100%) on E168's forecast change from the latest survey level. Pushing it up: Climate Stress 45%, Employment (national) 9%, Market / Prices 5%, Fish Kill (fisheries production proxy) 1%. They show what moved the model, not causes. Poverty and density (used for the city and municipal ranking) and forecast timing account for another 40% of that influence.

blocks.label: Figure 1
blocks.title: Factors Behind the Risk Probability in Quezon, 2027 Q1
blocks.note: Red bars pushed E168's forecast change up, green bars pulled it down; groups with no effect are not shown. Relative model influence, not causes.

blocks.text: News behind the 2027 Q1 estimate for Quezon: 6 article(s) from 2026-Q2, 2026-Q3: 6 classified relevant by the E60 classifier v2 (AI-evaluated, not human-validated; syndicated copies removed). Headlines only (the source gives no lead text). Collected retrospectively in October 2026 by publication date; the window was extended to earlier quarters because the evidence quarter had fewer than 5 articles.
By topic, they were about weather and climate (1 report), fisheries production (1 report), and food prices (1 report).

items: E168 food-insecurity risk forecast (probability of HIGH, HFIAS moderate+severe >= 50%) -- not an official food insecurity classification.

A forecast risk class, not a measured food-insecurity rate. It was validated on 72 provincial forecasts from 3 survey rounds (2018, 2019, 2021): accuracy 75.0% at one quarter ahead against 62.5% for the latest survey alone. It tends to over-predict by about 3 points (about 2 in 5 HIGH calls were false alarms) and rarely misses a HIGH province.
Lead 1: accuracy 0.750 on 72 provincial forecasts (latest survey alone 0.625), HIGH precision 0.59, recall 0.88, F1 0.71, AUC 0.89.
Lead 2: accuracy 0.778 on 72 provincial forecasts (latest survey alone 0.625), HIGH precision 0.63, recall 0.88, F1 0.73, AUC 0.89.
Lead 3: accuracy 0.750 on 72 provincial forecasts (latest survey alone 0.625), HIGH precision 0.60, recall 0.84, F1 0.70, AUC 0.87.

Acceptance rule (owner decision 2026-11-07, set after the results were known): accuracy of at least 75% and a Brier score significantly better than reusing the latest survey. Leads 1-3 meet it; Lead 4 (73.6%) does not.
Evidence limits: 72 forecasts from 3 survey rounds; only 5 are CALABARZON provinces (all observed LOW). Forecasts for the ENNS 2022 round are sealed (SHA-256 f8228fae).

City and municipal values are priority rankings within the province: the province probability re-weighted by poverty and population density, shown in the province's risk colour. They are not separate estimates for each city or municipality.
This is not an official food insecurity classification. The report presents findings only; it does not recommend actions and should be used alongside DA Region IV-A's own guidance.
